title: は particle (topic)
explanation: Marks the topic of a sentence. Often read as 'wa' when used as a particle.
kana: わたしはがくせいです。
mistakes: Do not confuse は topic marker with は as the syllable 'ha' inside words.

title: を particle (object)
explanation: Marks the direct object of a verb.
mistakes: を is pronounced 'o' as a particle.

quiz.q: Choose the object particle: パン___食べます。

title: です / だ (to be)
explanation: です is polite; だ is plain/casual. Used to state identity or description.
mistakes: Use です in polite contexts; avoid mixing plain and polite in the same sentence.

title: て form
explanation: Verb form used for requests, connecting actions, progressive, and more.
mistakes: Te-form conjugation depends on verb group.

title: ように (so that / like)
explanation: Used to express purpose, change, or similarity depending on context.
example: 忘れないようにメモします。
kana: わすれないようにメモします。
meaning: I'll take notes so I don't forget.
mistakes: Distinguish from ために (direct purpose with volitional control).

title: わけではない
explanation: Means 'it's not that...' or 'it doesn't mean...'; partial denial.
kana: きらいなわけではない。
meaning: It's not that I dislike it.
mistakes: It softens denial; not a strong absolute negation.

title: を皮切りに
explanation: Starting with...; used when an event triggers a series of developments.
example: 東京公演を皮切りに全国ツアーが始まった。
kana: とうきょうこうえんをかわきりにぜんこくツアーがはじまった。
romaji: Toukyou kouen wo kawakiri ni zenkoku tsuaa ga hajimatta.
meaning: Starting with the Tokyo performance, a nationwide tour began.
